disclaimer: Rules summarise widely taught horticultural knowledge and the cited reviews. They are decision support, not validated agronomic prescriptions. Verify against local extension-service guidance and cultivar information.

evidence_sources.broussard2023: Broussard, Coates & Martinsen (2023) Artificial Pollination Technologies: A Review. Agronomy 13(5):1351. doi:10.3390/agronomy13051351
evidence_sources.singh2025: Singh, Seneviratne & Hussain (2025) A comprehensive review of current robot-based pollinators for crop pollination. Artificial Intelligence Review 59:26. doi:10.1007/s10462-025-11409-1
evidence_sources.zhang2025: Zhang et al. (2025) A comprehensive review of autonomous flower pollination techniques. Computers and Electronics in Agriculture. doi:10.1016/j.compag.2025.110577
evidence_sources.textbook: Standard horticultural / floral-biology knowledge (not tied to a single study); verify locally.

temperature_c.note: Pollen germination, tube growth and insect flight are commonly reduced outside roughly this range; crop-specific limits differ.

relative_humidity_pct.note: Very high humidity can make pollen clump and stay in anthers; very low humidity can desiccate stigmas.

rain_mm_h.note: Rain washes pollen and stops insect activity.

wind_kmh.note: Strong wind reduces bee foraging and makes precise transfer harder.

species.flower_type: perfect (hermaphrodite), pendant, yellow; anthers fused into a cone around the style
species.mechanism_detail: Poricidal anthers release pollen when the flower is vibrated (buzz pollination by bumblebees; vibrating wands or air pulses in greenhouses). No external pollen supply is needed.
species.reproductive_characteristics: Stigma sits inside or just beyond the anther cone; pollen release requires vibration.
species.strategy: Vibrate open flower trusses (e.g. electric pollination wand or supervised bumblebee hives) when flowers are fully open; repeat every 2-3 days during flowering.
limitations: Heat stress can make pollen non-viable even when flowers look fully open.
Cultivar and greenhouse climate strongly change outcomes.

species.flower_type: perfect, purple, often solitary; poricidal anthers around the style
species.compatibility: largely self-compatible; some cross-pollination by insects
species.mechanism_detail: Like tomato, anthers open by apical pores; vibration releases pollen. Flowers differ in style length (long, medium, short/pseudo-short styled); long- and medium-styled flowers set fruit far more reliably.
species.reproductive_characteristics: Style length relative to the anther cone matters for fruit set.
species.strategy: Gently vibrate fully open, long/medium-styled flowers; short-styled flowers are poor candidates regardless of timing.
limitations: Style-length class cannot currently be measured by POLLINEX from images.

species.flower_type: perfect, small, white to purple-tinged; anthers dehisce longitudinally
species.mechanism_detail: Mostly self-pollinated; insects increase pollen transfer and can raise fruit set and seed number. Gentle shaking or brushing can assist in protected cultivation.
species.reproductive_characteristics: Stigma usually at or slightly above anther level.
species.strategy: Light brushing or gentle shaking of open flowers in the morning; for seed purity, bag flowers to prevent insect outcrossing.
limitations: Cross-pollination between hot and sweet types can occur and is not modelled.

species.flower_type: perfect, white-pink, in clusters of ~5 with a central 'king' flower opening first
species.compatibility: mostly self-incompatible (gametophytic S-RNase); needs compatible pollen from another cultivar with overlapping bloom
species.mechanism_detail: Honeybees and other insects carry compatible pollen between cultivars; supplemental hand/blower/spray application of collected compatible pollen is used where pollinizers or bees are lacking.
species.reproductive_characteristics: Five styles; stigmas receptive for a few days after opening.
species.strategy: Ensure a compatible pollinizer cultivar or apply collected compatible pollen to newly opened (especially king) flowers; same-cultivar pollen will not work.
limitations: Cultivar compatibility (S-alleles) cannot be inferred from images.

species.flower_type: perfect, white, in corymbs; red-purple anthers
species.mechanism_detail: Pear nectar is low in sugar so flowers are comparatively unattractive to honeybees; supplemental pollen application (including electrostatic) has improved fruit set under poor conditions.
species.reproductive_characteristics: Five styles; receptivity lasts only a few days.
visual_readiness_cues: anthers still red-purple, not yet shrivelled
species.strategy: Provide compatible pollinizer bloom overlap or apply compatible pollen to freshly opened flowers; consider extra hive density because bees under-visit pear.
limitations: Compatibility groups cannot be determined from images.

species.flower_type: perfect, pink, solitary or paired, appearing before leaves
species.compatibility: most cultivars self-fertile; a few are male-sterile and need pollinizers
species.mechanism_detail: Self-pollen suffices for most cultivars, but insect visits improve transfer from anthers to stigma; male-sterile cultivars need pollen from another cultivar.
species.reproductive_characteristics: Single pistil surrounded by many stamens.
species.strategy: Normally rely on self-pollination plus insects; brush-transfer within the flower can supplement in poor weather. For male-sterile cultivars, apply pollen from a fertile cultivar.
limitations: Male-sterile cultivars cannot be recognised from images.

species.flower_type: mostly perfect, white with a yellow receptacle covered in many pistils
species.mechanism_detail: Each pistil (future achene) must be fertilised; incomplete pollination gives misshapen fruit. Insects, air movement or brushing improve coverage of the receptacle.
species.reproductive_characteristics: Hundreds of pistils on a domed receptacle; stamens ring the receptacle.
species.strategy: Distribute pollen over the whole receptacle (insects, gentle air flow, soft brush). Even coverage matters more than quantity.
limitations: Per-pistil fertilisation cannot be seen in images.

species.flower_type: capitulum (head) of hundreds of disc florets surrounded by sterile ray florets
species.compatibility: variable; many modern hybrids partly self-compatible, older types largely self-incompatible
species.mechanism_detail: Disc florets are protandrous (pollen presented before the same floret's stigma opens) and open in rings from the edge toward the centre over several days, so a head carries florets at different stages.
species.reproductive_characteristics: Readiness is per floret ring, not per head.
visual_readiness_cues: ring of florets with exposed stigmas moving inward
species.strategy: Support bee visitation over the multi-day flowering of each head; for hand transfer, rub pollen across the ring of florets with receptive stigmas on successive days.
limitations: Per-ring floret stage is not detected; head-level stage is an approximation.

species.flower_type: large perfect flower; stamens fused into a staminal column with five stigma pads at its tip
species.mechanism_detail: Pollen from the column's anthers is transferred onto the five stigma pads above them, by insects/birds or by hand (breeders dab pollen from a chosen donor onto the stigma pads).
species.reproductive_characteristics: Individual flowers typically last about one day, so the window is short.
species.strategy: On the day the flower is fully open, transfer pollen (self or chosen donor) onto the five stigma pads; act early because the flower closes the same day.
limitations: Many cultivars set little or no seed; visual readiness does not imply fertility.
